record.scholarship_name: TSLS Scholarships for High Achievers Higher Education (Level 7) Overseas Scheme
record.provider: Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service (TSLS), Fiji
record.description: TSLS describes this as an existing merit-based scheme for degree programmes under the national priority areas not offered locally. It funds 80 Fiji citizens who scored 340/400 or above in Year 13 to study a listed bachelor's degree at one of 20 named Australian and New Zealand universities.
record.existing_notes: Live research completed 2026-10-10 on tsls.com.fj. Funding figures come from section 2.4 (p.45) of the 2026 TSLS Scholarship Policies Handbook; the scheme page names 80 awards and eligible institutions but publishes no amount or closing date. The live scheme page returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-10, so its content was read from the 27 September 2026 capture of that official URL and cross-checked against the 2026 Handbook. The 2027 Handbook (September 2026) no longer lists this scheme, so the 2026 round (closed 31 January 2026) is the last published cycle.
record.deadline_display: 31 January 2026 (last published round, 2026 academic year; next round not yet published)
record.deadline_note: No closing date is published on the scheme page. For the 2026 academic year round, TSLS announced applications opened on 5 December 2025 and set the closing date at 31 January. TSLS opens applications before each academic year; one national deadline applies, with no separate institutional deadline.
record.study_mode: Full-time: sponsored students must enrol in the full academic load required by the institution's academic regulations, and may not work full-time or part-time without TSLS approval.
record.citizenship_residency: Fiji citizen, and ordinarily resident in Fiji for at least three (3) years before the award commencement date unless determined by the Service.
record.international_eligibility: No - Fiji citizens only; applicants must also be ordinarily resident in Fiji for at least three years.
record.subject_or_agency_requirement: Yes - the application must be for a listed priority discipline and programme under the Overseas Scholarship at one of the 20 named eligible universities in Australia and New Zealand, supported by a final offer letter.
record.academic_requirements: Completed Year 13 in 2025 (or as determined by the Service at the time of application) with an aggregate score of 340/400 or above. Applicants who completed Foundation Studies or repeated Year 13 are not eligible.
eligibility: Be ordinarily resident in Fiji for at least three (3) years before the award commencement date, unless determined by the Service.
Have completed Year 13 in 2025 (or as determined by the Service at the time of application); Foundation Studies completers and Year 13 repeaters are not eligible.
Score 340/400 and above in the Year 13 examination and apply in a listed programme for Overseas Scholarship.
Secure a place at an eligible institution by means of a final offer letter.
Not be an existing TSLS sponsored student or graduate (on active bond service) or sponsored through any other agency.
requirements: Final (not provisional) offer letter from one of the 20 eligible universities in Australia or New Zealand.
Final Year 13 examination results showing an aggregate of 340/400 or above.
Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and a digital passport-size photo.
Bank account, M-PAiSA or MyCash details, with a supporting statement where applicable, for allowance payment.
Parents' payslip or statutory declaration of income where applicable; medical report, parental death certificate and guardianship letter where applicable.
documents: Final offer letter from the eligible institution (medical report where applicable)
Bank account / M-PAiSA / MyCash details with statement where applicable
Highest qualification result; parents' payslip or statutory declaration (death certificate and guardianship letter where applicable)
benefits: Tuition Fee and General Service Fee, paid by TSLS directly to the institution.
Living allowance at a maximum rate of AUD or NZD $38,400.
Economy class airfare at commencement, one return trip on completion of 50% of studies, and a return fare after completion/graduation.
Visa fees up to FJD $3,000 and overseas student health cover for the sponsored student only.
One-off establishment allowance of up to AUD/NZD $3,500 at the start of the programme and excess baggage allowance of up to AUD/NZD $300.
record.selection_criteria: Merit ranking from the highest Year 13 aggregate downward until each scheme quota is filled; no interview or aptitude test is published for this scheme. TSLS assesses applications against the stated criteria and its decision is final and cannot be appealed. 80 awards are allocated across seven priority disciplines (Information Technology 20; Engineering, Medical & Health, Agriculture/Forestry & Fisheries, Science & Innovation, Business & Commerce and Special Areas 10 each).
record.selection_notes: 80 awards across seven priority disciplines: Information Technology Services 20; Engineering Services 10; Medical & Health Services 10; Agriculture, Forestry & Fisheries 10; Science and Innovation 10; Business and Commerce 10; Special Areas 10. Published programme examples include nine engineering specialisations, Speech Therapy/Sports Medicine/Prosthetics & Orthosis, Veterinary Sciences/Aquaculture/Biosecurity, Software Engineering/Cyber Security/AI & Data Science, Meteorology, BCom in Actuarial Finance or Forensic Accounting, and Forensic Science/Quantity Surveying.
record.application_method: Online only via the TSLS Apply portal (https://apply.tsls.com.fj): register with a personal Gmail, Yahoo or Hotmail address and verify the account, complete every task and mark each complete, then accept the declaration to submit. Registration can start before Year 13 results, but submission needs final results and a final offer letter; late or incomplete applications are not assessed.
record.application_route: 100% online via the TSLS Apply portal; in-person help at TSLS offices in Suva, Lautoka, Nadi and Labasa (including self-service kiosks), by email to mytsls@tsls.com.fj or by phone on (+679) 8921240.
record.application_period: Last published round: 5 December 2025 - 31 January 2026 (2026 Academic Term 1); TSLS opens applications before each academic year.
record.post_award_obligations: Bonded award: awardees must accept the offer letter and acceptance agreement and sign the bond in the application portal. Under the 2027 TSLS Handbook, bond service for merit-based schemes with overseas study is the number of years sponsored x 2.5 (a four-year degree therefore carries a 10-year bond), and choosing not to serve means repaying the total amount disbursed. Guarantors must meet TSLS's salary bands based on total debt disbursed, are placed on the Immigration Stop Departure List while the student studies overseas, and students need a temporary travel release for overseas trips before the bond is cleared.
record.status_note: The last published round (2026 academic year) opened on 5 December 2025 and closed on 31 January 2026. When checked on 2026-10-10 the TSLS Apply portal showed no open application programs, the scheme page was returning HTTP 404, and the 2027 TSLS Handbook (September 2026) no longer lists this scheme. No next-round announcement was found on the pages checked - monitor tsls.com.fj and TSLS social media, or call (+679) 8921240.
record.program_type: Government scholarship - Fiji Government merit-based scheme.
record.host_institution_restriction: Yes - 20 named universities only: Auckland University of Technology; CQ University Australia; Griffith University; Massey University; Monash University; Queensland University of Technology; Swinburne University of Technology; University of Auckland; University of Canberra; University of Canterbury; University of Newcastle; UNSW; University of Queensland; University of Sydney; University of Waikato; Victoria University of Wellington; Western Sydney University; University of Otago; RMIT University; University of Southern Queensland.

applicant_utility.summary: TSLS sends 80 Fiji Year 13 leavers who scored 340/400 or above to listed bachelor's degrees at 20 named Australian and New Zealand universities, covering tuition, general service fees, visa fees, overseas health cover, airfare, an establishment allowance and a living allowance capped at AUD or NZD $38,400. It is a national, merit-ranked, bond-backed award applied for entirely online through the TSLS Apply portal, with the last published round running from 5 December 2025 to 31 January 2026. Expect a long bond obligation (2.5 years of service per year sponsored) and a capped living allowance to compare with real costs in your host city before accepting.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Fiji citizens who completed Year 13 in 2025 with an aggregate of 340/400 or higher, targeting one of the seven listed priority disciplines (engineering, medical and health services, agriculture/forestry/fisheries, information technology, meteorology, business and commerce, or the special areas list) at one of the 20 named universities, and who hold or can quickly secure a final offer letter. Not a fit if you completed Foundation Studies, repeated Year 13, are already TSLS-sponsored or serving a bond, are sponsored by another agency, have been ordinarily resident in Fiji for under three years, or want a programme or university not on the scheme's lists.
application_readiness_checklist: Register early at https://apply.tsls.com.fj using your own Gmail, Yahoo or Hotmail address, then verify and activate the account from the email link.
Start registration before Year 13 results are released, but do not submit until you hold final results and a final offer letter - provisional offers are rejected.
Scan every document to PDF, PNG or JPG and keep file sizes small; the Know How To Apply page caps uploads at 5MB per file while the 2027 Handbook states 20MB, so aim under 5MB.
Confirm your programme appears in the scheme's priority discipline list and your university is one of the 20 eligible institutions before paying any university application fees.
Complete every task in the portal and click Mark as Complete on each one, then accept the declaration to submit - late or incomplete applications are not assessed.
Track progress under My Application and watch the email address used at registration for the TSLS outcome.
If offered, sign and upload the Provisional Offer Letter and Bond Form within 3 days of the date on the offer letter, or the offer lapses.
Line up a guarantor early who meets TSLS's salary band requirements, and note guarantors are placed on the Immigration Stop Departure List.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting a provisional offer letter - TSLS states these are not accepted for processing, and a completed application requires the final offer letter.
Missing the 31 January closing date: late applications are not considered for assessment.
Choosing a programme that is not in the scheme's priority discipline list, or a university outside the 20 eligible institutions.
Being a Foundation Studies completer or a Year 13 repeater - both are explicitly excluded.
Being an existing TSLS-sponsored student or graduate on active bond service, or sponsored by any other agency.
An aggregate below 340/400 in the Year 13 examination.
Leaving mandatory fields or tasks incomplete, or failing the three-year ordinary residency requirement.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: TSLS publishes no itemised list of costs an awardee must still meet. Budget for: living expenses above the AUD/NZD 38,400 maximum living allowance and the one-off AUD/NZD 3500 establishment allowance; university application fees; visa medicals, police clearance and immigration costs beyond the FJD 3,000 visa cap; laptop, textbooks and course materials; extra flights home beyond the single return trip covered at the 50% completion point; local transport and phone costs; and full repayment of everything disbursed if you later decide not to serve the bond.
document_audit: Final offer letter: provisional letters are explicitly not accepted, so wait for the eligible institution's final letter and check the programme name matches the scheme's priority list.
Year 13 results: TSLS needs the official final examination result, not an annual school report; the last round accepted results from the 2025 Year 13 examination.
TIN: apply for your Taxpayer Identification Number before the window opens if you do not already have one.
Birth certificate: get a clean, legible scan; a certified copy is safer than a phone photo of the original.
Bank or mobile money details: have your bank account, M-PAiSA or MyCash details ready with a statement where applicable, since allowances are paid into the nominated account.

Income and guardianship papers: parents' payslip or statutory declaration where applicable, and death certificate plus guardianship letter if you live in care. Scan each page as PDF, PNG or JPG within the size cap.
alerts: Timing: the last published round opened 5 December 2025 and closed 31 January 2026; TSLS opens applications before each academic year, so watch tsls.com.fj and TSLS social media from late November for the next intake.
Offers expire fast: every scholarship offer must be accepted within 3 days of the date stated in the offer letter, and unaccepted offers are declined.

Bond exposure: for merit-based schemes with overseas study the bond is the number of years sponsored x 2.5, so a 4-year degree means a 10-year obligation, and opting out means repaying all disbursed funds.
Guarantors must meet salary bands tied to total debt disbursed and are listed on the Immigration Stop Departure List while you study overseas; obtain a temporary travel release for any overseas trip.

Academic conditions: one programme, major or institution change only, and before the third term. Each term is reviewed; missing the GPA or pass rate triggers probation, then tuition-only probation, then suspension.

verification.notes: All figures were taken from pages on the awarding body's own domain (tsls.com.fj), with no aggregators or news reports used. The funding amount and benefit set come directly from the 2026 TSLS Scholarship Policies Handbook PDF hosted on tsls.com.fj (section 2.4, p.45), which lists the privileges shared by the High Achievers Higher Education (Level 7) Overseas Scheme. The live scheme page failed to load (HTTP 404, verified in a browser) after two direct fetch attempts and a browser load, so its content was read from the 27 September 2026 capture of that exact official URL and cross-checked against the 2026 Handbook. Tuition, living allowance, travel, visa and health cover are stated in the handbook; the handbook does not say whether the AUD/NZD 38,400 living allowance is a yearly or whole-programme maximum rate, so funding_period is null. Currency is published as either AUD or NZD depending on the host country, so no single ISO code applies. The 2026 round closed on 31 January 2026; as at 2026-10-10 the TSLS Apply portal showed no open programs and the 2027 Handbook no longer lists this scheme, so the status is CLOSED with no confirmed next round.
